options: Exactly 30 days after StartDate
The last day of the current month, ignoring the second argument
The last day of the month one month after StartDate
The first day of the month after StartDate
questions.explain: EOMONTH's second argument offsets by whole months and always returns a month-end date — 1 means the end of the following month, correctly accounting for how many days that month has.

questions.q: Why is DATEDIF worth knowing even though Excel doesn't show it in formula autocomplete?
options: It has been officially deprecated and should never be used
It's a real, fully working function for calculating years/months/days between two dates — it's just undocumented in the UI
It requires a special add-in to function
It only works in Excel for the web, not desktop
questions.explain: DATEDIF calculates precise durations in years, months, or days between two dates and works perfectly when typed — Microsoft simply doesn't surface it in autocomplete or the function wizard.

questions.q: Why would you use TEXT instead of just referencing a formatted cell directly in a concatenation?
options: TEXT converts text back into a number
TEXT is required before any number can be summed
There's no difference — referencing the cell directly always preserves formatting in a concatenation
Concatenating a raw number strips its display formatting, so TEXT is needed to keep formatting like currency symbols or date patterns when joining it into a string
questions.explain: When a number or date is joined into a text string with &, its cell formatting is lost and the raw value shows instead — TEXT explicitly reapplies a format code so the concatenated result displays correctly.

questions.q: What is a classic, silent cause of VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP returning #N/A even though the values look identical?
options: Invisible leading or trailing spaces in the lookup value, which TRIM removes
The lookup table having too many columns
EOMONTH being used somewhere else in the workbook
Using LEFT instead of RIGHT
questions.explain: Extra spaces from imported or pasted data are invisible to the eye but break exact-match comparisons — TRIM strips them so the lookup can match correctly.

questions.q: What is the difference between LEFT/RIGHT and MID?
options: There is no functional difference between them
LEFT and RIGHT require a starting position argument that MID does not
MID can only be used on numbers, never on text
LEFT and RIGHT pull a fixed number of characters from the start or end of a string; MID pulls a chunk from the middle given a starting position and length
questions.explain: LEFT/RIGHT anchor to one end of the string and take a count of characters; MID needs both a starting position and a length since it can extract from anywhere in the middle.
